profile.summary: CPA (Compositional Perturbation Autoencoder) is a deep generative model that predicts how single cells respond to drugs and genetic perturbations, alone or in combination. It is trained on a perturbation dataset of single-cell expression with perturbation, dose and covariate labels, and predicts expression for unseen combinations of perturbations, doses and cell types, with interpretable perturbation and covariate embeddings.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper Abstract and synopsis; README.md: What is CPA?

summary_quotes.text: is a deep learning model for predicting the transcriptomic responses of single cells to single or combinatorial treatments from drugs and genetic manipulations
Out-of-distribution predictions of unseen drug and gene combinations at various doses and among different cell types.
Learn interpretable drug and cell-type latent spaces.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: An encoder network decomposes each cell's expression into additive latent embeddings for its basal state, the observed perturbations and the observed covariates. An adversarial discriminator is trained against the encoder so the basal state carries no perturbation or covariate information, which lets embeddings be recombined at prediction time. Perturbation embeddings are scaled by a neural network of the dose or time. A decoder maps the recombined latent state back to expression.

quotes.text: the CPA first uses an encoder neural network to decompose the cells' gene expression into a series of learnable, additive embeddings, which correspond to its basal state, the observed perturbation, and the observed covariates
By virtue of an adversarial loss, these embeddings are independent of each other, so they can be recombined at prediction time to predict the effect of novel perturbation
the learned embeddings about each perturbation are scaled nonlinearly via a neural network which receives the continuous covariate values for each cell

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: CPA learns from a given single-cell perturbation dataset; the README's preprocessing recipe prepares the user's own dataset for it. The current implementation is the cpa-tools package in theislab/cpa, whose hyperparameter tuner is based on the scvi-tools optimiser; datasets and pre-trained models are in a Google Drive folder linked from the README. The paper's analyses are in a separate reproducibility repository. A result should name the package version or commit, the training dataset and the hyperparameters.

sections.title: Intended uses
sections.body: Predicting responses to unseen drug and gene combinations and doses, transferring perturbation effects to unseen cell types, estimating dose-response curves, and removing batch effects in latent and expression space.

quotes.text: Estimate the dose-response curve for each perturbation and their combinations.
Transfer pertubration effects from on cell-type to an unseen cell-type.

run_guide.summary: Create a conda environment, install PyTorch, CPA and scanpy, and preprocess a perturbation dataset for training; training and prediction follow the tutorials, which were not reviewed.
prerequisites: A single-cell perturbation dataset with raw counts and perturbation and dose labels.

steps.title: Create an environment
steps.shell:
conda create -n cpa python=3.9
conda activate cpa
pip install torch==1.13.1+cpu --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
steps.explanation: The documentation's environment and CPU-only PyTorch commands; use a CUDA build from the same page if you have a GPU.

steps.title: Install CPA and scanpy
steps.shell:
pip install git+https://github.com/theislab/cpa
pip install scanpy
steps.explanation: Installs the latest CPA from GitHub (not pinned to the reviewed commit) and scanpy.

steps.title: Preprocess your dataset
steps.shell:
python - <<'EOF'
import scanpy as sc
# adata: your perturbation AnnData with perturbation and dosage in adata.obs
sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_counts=100)
adata.layers['counts'] = adata.X.copy()
sc.pp.normalize_total(adata, target_sum=1e4, exclude_highly_expressed=True)
sc.pp.log1p(adata)
sc.pp.highly_variable_genes(adata, n_top_genes=5000, subset=True)
EOF
steps.explanation: The README's preprocessing recipe wrapped in a heredoc by Rewire. It does not load data: add your own line that creates adata, and save the result with adata.write_h5ad.

outputs: A preprocessed AnnData ready for CPA training; the README gives no training or prediction command.
